_comment_scope: A CURATED SUBSET, deliberately: only the tests that can kill mutants in the
modules below, because `coverageAnalysis: off` makes every mutant re-run the
whole command. That design has one failure mode, and Miguel hit it on PR #42:
a module added to `mutate` whose tests were never added to the command scores
against a suite that cannot see it, and the report does not say so.
So the rule when touching either list: a file in `mutate` must have its tests
in `command`, and adding a test file here is how a new module earns its place.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT: test/renderer-scope.test.js and the repo-scanning tests.
Their subject is the REPOSITORY rather than a function -- the shared-scope
allow-list fails on Stryker's own instrumentation globals, and the
git-ls-files and control-character guards assert about the file tree, which
Stryker's sandbox is a copy of. They kill no mutant, because nothing they
assert is an expression a mutator can reach.
_comment_rule_is_enforced: THE RULE ABOVE IS NOW A TEST, because I broke it by hand twice in the two
commits immediately after writing it. Mortimer found six test files that
exercise mutated modules and were absent from `command` -- including the two
newest, which are where H1-H5 and I1 are tested, so the most recently changed
code on the branch was being measured against a suite that could not see its
tests. Those kills existed; Stryker was never told to run them.
A rule written in a comment is a rule nothing enforces. See
test/stryker-config.test.js: every module in `mutate` must have every test
file that requires it present in `command`, derived by reading the requires
rather than by restating the list.

_comment_timeout: RAISED from 20000 for PR #42. app/secret-vault.js now derives keys with
scrypt at N=2^17, ~200ms per derivation by design, and STRYKER COUNTS A
TIMEOUT AS KILLED -- so a timeout is a PHANTOM KILL, the exact mirror of the
phantom survivor, and a comfortable score can be made of clocks rather than
assertions. Miguel raised this before the run rather than after.
Two mitigations, both applied: the lock suites inject cheap parameters
(N=1024) and a short file-lock deadline, so only the handful of tests that
deliberately exercise the REAL cost pay it; and the ceiling is high enough
that a mutant slowing a derivation still finishes and is judged on assertions.
READ THE TIMEOUT COUNT IN THE REPORT, not only the score.
